If a soil sample has a void ratio of \( e = 1.3 \), determine its porosity \( n \).
references:
FE Reference Handbook 10.5 P259:

Use the relationship between porosity and void ratio:

    \[

\begin{align}

n &= \frac{e}{1 + e} \\

&= \frac{1.3}{1 + 1.3} \\

&= 0.57

\end{align}

\]

Assuming the remaining area is rock, and excavation costs are \( \$120 / \mathrm{ft}^2 \) for sandy silt and \( \$350 / \mathrm{ft}^2 \) for rock. Determine the expected total foundation excavation cost. The cost is most nearly:

A ball starts from rest and slides down a \(30^\circ\) incline. After \(4\ \text{s}\) its speed reaches \(6\ \text{m/s}\). Assuming constant acceleration along the plane, how far will the block travel in the next  \(6\ \text{s}\)?

A test vehicle moves along a circular ramp of radius \(r=40\ \text{m}\). Determine the magnitude of the acceleration (in \(\text{m/s}^2\)).

A block initially at rest is acted upon by a constant horizontal force of \(18\ \text{N}\) for \(3\ \text{s}\). Determine the mass of the block in kilograms.

A soccer ball is kicked from level ground with initial speed \(v_0 = 40\ \text{m/s}\) at an angle \(\theta = 45^\circ\) above the horizontal. Neglect air resistance and use \(g = 9.81\ \text{m/s}^2\). Find the horizontal range \(R\).

A car is traveling along a straight highway at a speed of \(72\ \text{km/h}\). It comes to rest uniformly in a distance of \(200\ \text{m}\). Find the stopping time \(t\) in seconds.

A small remote-controlled boat needs to cross a 120 m wide lake. In still air, the boat can travel straight across in 3 minutes. Under these conditions, it takes 4 minutes to cross. What is the wind’s velocity in m/min?
A cyclist rides from home to a lakeside trail at \(12\ \text{mph}\) and returns along the same route at \(18\ \text{mph}\). What is the average speed (mph) for the entire round trip?

A small object moves along a straight path with uniform acceleration \(a_0 = 4\ \text{cm/s}^2\). During the 10th second, it travels \(43\ \text{cm}\). Determine the initial velocity \(v_0\) in \(\text{cm/s}\).
A commuter train moves at 54 km/h and comes to rest uniformly in 12 s. Determine how far from the platform the brakes should be applied.

A cargo drone flies horizontally at \(100\ \text{m/s}\) and drops a small package from an altitude of \(300\ \text{m}\). Neglecting air resistance, what will be the package’s speed (m/s) after \(4\ \text{s}\) of free fall? Use \(g = 9.81\ \text{m/s}^2\).

A rescue drone flying horizontally at a constant altitude of \(400\ \text{m}\) releases a supply package with a horizontal speed of \(120\ \text{m/s}\). Neglecting air resistance, how far horizontally (m) will the package travel before it reaches the ground?  Assume \(g = 9.81\ \text{m/s}^2\).

A drone releases a small package vertically upward from a height with an initial speed of \(10\ \text{m/s}\). After \(4\ \text{s}\), the package reaches the ground. Assuming \(g = 9.81\ \text{m/s}^2\), find the release height \(h\) (m) of the drone.

A race car moves along a curved test track described by \(y = 0.05\,x^{2}\). At the point where \(x = 200\ \text{m}\), its speed is \(v = 25\ \text{m/s}\) and its tangential acceleration is \(a_t = 3\ \text{m/s}^2\). Determine the magnitude of the acceleration at this instant.

Determine the magnitude of the net impulse (in kg·m/s) delivered to the ball by the player’s foot.

A \(0.5\ \text{kg}\) drone is flying horizontally toward the east with a speed of \(12\ \text{m/s}\). questions.answer: \(2.67\ \text{m/s}\) in the travel direction of the truck (north).

but are provided for context.)

Annual interest rate: \(3\%\)

Annual maintenance (paid at year end): \(\$420\)

Using the straight-line method, determine the total depreciation of the equipment for the first \( 5 \, \mathrm{years} \). The total depreciation is most nearly:

A company purchased a piece of heavy equipment with an initial cost of \( \$10,000 \). The annual interest rate is \( 2.5\% \). The equipment requires annual maintenance costing \( \$400 \), which is paid at the end of each year. Using the Modified Accelerated Cost Recovery System (MACRS), determine the total depreciation for the equipment during the first \( 3 \, \mathrm{years} \) of operation, assuming a \( 10 \)-year recovery period. The total depreciation is most nearly:

An agricultural business purchases a new tractor for \( \$50,000 \). The tractor qualifies for a \( 10 \)-year MACRS recovery period. What is the approximate book value of the tractor at the exact end of the \( 10 \)-year recovery period (end of year \( 10 \))?

A company buys computer software with an initial cost of \( \$60,000 \). It qualifies for a \( 3 \)-year MACRS recovery period. What is the approximate book value of the software at the end of year \( 2 \)?

A manufacturing plant purchases a new machine for \( \$120,000 \). The machine has an estimated salvage value of \( \$20,000 \) after its \( 10 \)-year useful life. Using straight-line depreciation, what is the book value of the machine at the end of year \( 4 \)?

A corporation has a gross income of \( \$300,000 \) and ordinary operating expenses of \( \$100,000 \) for the current year. During this same year, the corporation purchased new manufacturing equipment for \( \$80,000 \). The equipment qualifies for a \( 5 \)-year MACRS recovery period. If the corporate income tax rate is \( 21\% \), what is the total income tax paid for this first year?

For a given tax year, a business has a total gross income of \( \$200,000 \). The business incurred \( \$60,000 \) in ordinary expenses. Earlier in the year, they purchased a piece of capital equipment for \( \$150,000 \), which has a \( 6 \)-year useful life and a \( \$30,000 \) salvage value. Using the straight-line method for depreciation, what is the taxable income for this first year?

A company bought an equipment for $5,000. The annual maintenance fee is $500 and continues indefinitely. If the interest rate is 5% per year, determine the present worth of all expenditures.
Initial cost: \(P_0=\$5{,}000\)

Annual maintenance: \(A=\$500/\text{yr}\) (perpetuity)

Interest rate: \(i=5\%=0.05\)

A bike was purchased with an initial cost of \( \$1,300 \) and an annual maintenance cost of \( \$250 \), which continues indefinitely. The interest rate is \( 6\% \). Determine the present worth of all expenditures.

A bond has a face value of \( \$5,000 \) and pays a nominal annual coupon rate of \( 6\% \), with payments made semi-annually. The bond matures in \( 10 \, \mathrm{years} \). If the required nominal interest rate is \( 8\% \) per year, what is the approximate value of the bond?

An investor purchases a bond for \( \$8,403 \). The bond has a face value of \( \$10,000 \), pays an annual coupon of \( \$400 \), and matures in \( 5 \, \mathrm{years} \). What is the approximate computed bond yield (interest rate)?

A bond has a face value of \( \$10,000 \), pays a uniform annual interest coupon of \( 5\% \), and matures in \( 10 \, \mathrm{years} \). If an investor’s required interest rate (yield) is \( 8\% \), what is the approximate value (present worth) of the bond?

An engineer invests \( \$20,000 \) in a long-term savings investment that guarantees a payout of exactly \( \$31,876 \) at the end of \( 8 \, \mathrm{years} \). What is the exact annual rate of return on this investment?

A company is considering a project that requires an initial investment of \( \$50,000 \) and provides uniform annual benefits of \( \$13,000 \) for \( 5 \, \mathrm{years} \). The company’s Minimum Acceptable Rate of Return (MARR) is \( 12\% \). What is the approximate rate of return, and should the project be accepted?

A proposed public park has an initial construction cost of \( \$50,000 \). The present worth of the expected annual public benefits is \( \$80,000 \), and the present worth of the annual maintenance costs is \( \$10,000 \). What is the benefit-cost ratio \( B/C \) for this project?

A construction project has potential weather delay costs with the following probability distribution: a \( 50\% \) chance of \( 0 \) days delay (\( \$0 \) cost), a \( 30\% \) chance of a \( 10 \)-day delay (\( \$10,000 \) cost), a \( 15\% \) chance of a \( 20 \)-day delay (\( \$25,000 \) cost), and a \( 5\% \) chance of a \( 30 \)-day delay (\( \$50,000 \) cost). What is the expected value of the delay cost?

An engineer is evaluating a decision tree with two paths. Path A requires an initial investment of \( \$20,000 \). It leads to a chance node with a \( 60\% \) probability of generating \( \$50,000 \) in revenue and a \( 40\% \) probability of generating \( \$10,000 \) in revenue. Path B requires an initial investment of \( \$10,000 \). It leads to a chance node with a \( 70\% \) probability of generating \( \$30,000 \) in revenue and a \( 30\% \) probability of generating \( \$5,000 \) in revenue. Which decision path should be chosen to maximize expected profit, and what is its expected value?

A business venture has a single chance node with three possible outcomes: a \( 40\% \) probability of a \( \$10,000 \) profit, a \( 35\% \) probability of a \( \$5,000 \) profit, and a \( 25\% \) probability of a \( \$2,000 \) loss. What is the expected value of this venture?

Measurements indicate that the air temperature decreases by \(12^\circ \mathrm{C}\) over a vertical height of \(1,000\ \mathrm{m}\) (Environmental Lapse Rate). Comparing this to the Dry Adiabatic Lapse Rate (\(\approx 9.8^\circ \mathrm{C/km}\)), how would you classify the atmospheric stability?

A parcel of dry air rises in the atmosphere. Assuming the process is adiabatic (no heat exchange), calculate the temperature at an elevation of \(2,000\ \mathrm{m}\) if the temperature at sea level (\(0\ \mathrm{m}\)) is \(25^\circ \mathrm{C}\). Use the standard Dry Adiabatic Lapse Rate (\(\Gamma_{AD}\)).

Stack gas analysis from an incinerator shows a Carbon Dioxide (\(CO_2\)) concentration of \(8.0\%\) by volume and a Carbon Monoxide (\(CO\)) concentration of \(80\ \mathrm{ppm}\) by volume. Calculate the Combustion Efficiency (CE).

A hazardous waste incinerator is fed a POHC (Principal Organic Hazardous Contaminant) at a rate of \(500\ \mathrm{kg/h}\). The mass emission rate of the same POHC in the stack gas is measured to be \(0.04\ \mathrm{kg/h}\). Calculate the Destruction and Removal Efficiency (DRE).

An ESP is required to achieve a collection efficiency of \(99\%\) (\(\eta = 0.99\)). The gas flow rate is \(500\ \mathrm{m^3/min}\) and the particle drift velocity is \(0.1\ \mathrm{m/s}\). Calculate the required total collection area (\(A\)).

An Electrostatic Precipitator (ESP) treats an air flow of \(10,000\ \mathrm{ft^3/min}\). The total collection plate area is \(4,000\ \mathrm{ft^2}\). The effective particle drift velocity is \(0.25\ \mathrm{ft/s}\). Calculate the fractional collection efficiency.

You are designing a Pulse Jet/Felt baghouse to collect Fly Ash. According to the “Air-to-Cloth Ratio for Baghouses” table in the FE Reference Handbook, what is the typical design Air-to-Cloth ratio in \(\mathrm{m^3/(min \cdot m^2)}\)?
A cyclone has a calculated cut diameter (\(d_{pc}\)) of \(10\ \mu\mathrm{m}\). Calculate the removal efficiency for particles with a diameter (\(d_p\)) of \(20\ \mu\mathrm{m}\).

Inlet width \(W = 0.25\ \mathrm{m}\)

Gas dynamic viscosity \(\mu = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{kg/(m \cdot s)}\)

Calculate the ground-level concentration along the plume centerline (\(y=0, z=0\)) in \(\mu \mathrm{g/m^3}\).

Determine the atmospheric stability class for a site with a surface wind speed of \(4.0\ \mathrm{m/s}\) during a clear summer day with strong solar insolation (sun high in the sky).

A contaminant has a Henry’s Law constant (\(H\)) of \(0.01\ \mathrm{atm \cdot m^3/kmol}\) at \(20^\circ \mathrm{C}\). Calculate the dimensionless Henry’s Law constant (\(H’\)).
(Use \(R = 0.0821\ \mathrm{m^3 \cdot atm/(kmol \cdot K)}\))

Alum (\(Al_2(SO_4)_3 \cdot 14H_2O\), MW \(\approx 594\)) is added to water at a dose of \(30\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). Based on the coagulation stoichiometry, how much alkalinity (expressed as \(CaCO_3\)) is consumed?

A sample of water has a Calcium Non-Carbonate Hardness (Permanent Hardness) of \(80\ \mathrm{mg/L}\) as \(CaCO_3\). Calculate the theoretical amount of Soda Ash (\(Na_2CO_3\)) required to remove this hardness.
(MW data: \(CaCO_3 = 100.1\), \(Na_2CO_3 = 106.0\))

A water source contains \(1.5\ \mathrm{mmol/L}\) of Magnesium Carbonate Hardness (\(Mg(HCO_3)_2\)). Calculate the stoichiometric amount of hydrated lime (\(Ca(OH)_2\), MW = \(74.1\ \mathrm{g/mol}\)) required to remove this magnesium.

Water analysis indicates a Calcium Carbonate Hardness of \(2.0\ \mathrm{mmol/L}\) (as \(Ca^{2+}\)). How much hydrated lime (\(Ca(OH)_2\), MW = \(74.1\ \mathrm{g/mol}\)) is required to remove this hardness stoichiometrically?

During the backwash of a rapid sand filter, the backwash velocity (\(v_B\)) is set to \(15\ \mathrm{m/hr}\). The terminal settling velocity (\(v_t\)) of the sand particles is determined to be \(180\ \mathrm{m/hr}\). Calculate the porosity of the fluidized bed (\(\eta_f\)).

A rapid sand filter has a bed depth of \(0.7\ \mathrm{m}\). The filtration rate (approach velocity) is \(300\ \mathrm{m/day}\). The sand grains have a diameter of \(0.6\ \mathrm{mm}\) and a drag coefficient (\(C_D\)) of \(5.0\). The porosity of the bed is \(0.4\). Using the Rose equation, calculate the head loss through the clean filter bed.

Determine the required CT value for 3-log (99.9%) inactivation of Giardia cysts by free chlorine under the following conditions:
Temperature: \(\le 0.5^\circ \mathrm{C}\)

pH: \(7.5\)

Chlorine Concentration: \(1.0\ \mathrm{mg/L}\)

A chlorine contact basin has a volume of \(20,000\ \mathrm{gallons}\) and the peak hourly flow rate is \(400\ \mathrm{gpm}\). The basin is classified as having “Superior” baffling conditions (\(BF = 0.7\)). Calculate the \(t_{10}\) time.

A disinfection process uses free chlorine. The residual chlorine concentration measured during peak hourly flow is \(1.5\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). The contact time \(t_{10}\) (time for 10% of water to pass) is determined to be \(90\ \mathrm{minutes}\). Calculate the \(CT_{calc}\) value.

A particle is settling in water with a calculated terminal velocity of \(0.1\ \mathrm{m/s}\). The particle diameter is \(0.5\ \mathrm{mm}\) (\(5 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m}\)). The kinematic viscosity of water is \(\nu = 1 \times 10^{-6}\ \mathrm{m^2/s}\). Calculate the Reynolds number and determine the flow regime.

A spherical sand particle with a diameter of \(0.1\ \mathrm{mm}\) (\(1 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m}\)) and a density of \(2,650\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}\) is settling in water at \(20^\circ \mathrm{C}\). The water density is \(\rho_f = 998\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}\) and the dynamic viscosity is \(\mu = 1.002 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{Pa \cdot s}\). Assuming laminar flow (Stokes’ Law applies), calculate the terminal settling velocity.
A clarifier has a volume of \(500\ \mathrm{m^3}\) and treats a wastewater flow of \(2,000\ \mathrm{m^3/day}\). What is the hydraulic residence time (\(\theta\)) in hours?

A rectangular sedimentation basin has a flow of \(6.0\ \mathrm{MGD}\). The basin is \(40\ \mathrm{ft}\) wide and has a water depth of \(10\ \mathrm{ft}\). Determine the horizontal velocity (\(v_h\)) in \(\mathrm{ft/min}\).

A circular secondary clarifier has a diameter of \(80\ \mathrm{ft}\). The influent flow rate is \(3.5\ \mathrm{MGD}\). Assuming the weir is located along the entire perimeter of the tank, calculate the weir loading rate (Weir Overflow Rate).
A circular clarifier with a diameter of \(60\ \mathrm{ft}\) treats a water flow of \(2.5\ \mathrm{MGD}\). What is the surface overflow rate?

A rectangular primary clarifier is designed to treat a water flow of \(4.0\ \mathrm{MGD}\). The basin dimensions are \(80\ \mathrm{ft}\) long, \(30\ \mathrm{ft}\) wide, and \(12\ \mathrm{ft}\) deep. Calculate the surface overflow rate in \(\mathrm{gpd/ft^2}\).

In a packed bed air stripper operating at \( 30^\circ\mathrm{C} \), a vapor contained in an air stream is dissolved in water. The Henry’s law constant (\( H \)) for the vapor-water system is \( 0.15 \, \mathrm{atm \cdot m^3/kmol} \). The volumetric flow rate of the air (\( Q_A \)) is \( 0.8 \, \mathrm{m^3/s} \). Determine the required volumetric flow rate of the water (\( Q_W \)). The water flow rate is most nearly:

A municipal wastewater treatment plant needs to reduce its effluent phosphorus concentration to meet new environmental discharge limits. The influent wastewater has a constant flow rate and contains a phosphate (\( \mathrm{PO_4^{3-}} \)) concentration of \( 20\,\mathrm{mg/L} \). The plant engineer plans to use aluminum sulfate (alum), \( \mathrm{Al_2(SO_4)_3 \cdot 14H_2O} \), to precipitate the phosphate as aluminum phosphate (\( \mathrm{AlPO_4} \)). Assuming theoretical stoichiometry governs the reaction and no other side reactions consume the coagulant, the required alum dose is most nearly:

An industrial plant is looking to utilize on-site waste streams as supplemental fuel for its boiler. To maximize energy output per unit mass, the plant engineer needs to identify the waste stream with the highest heating value. Which of the following materials offers the highest heating value (Btu/lb)?

A waste-to-energy facility is evaluating the potential heat output from processing municipal solid waste. If the facility processes \(1,000\ \mathrm{lbs}\) of source-separated Plastics, what is the estimated total energy content based on typical values?
For Nuclear Power Reactors, which reactor type typically has the highest thermal efficiency?
Determine the appropriate turbine type for a Head of \(500\ \mathrm{ft}\) and a Power Output of \(100,000\ \mathrm{kW}\).
According to the table “Noise of Different Activities…”, which of the following activities has a noise level closest to \(65\ \mathrm{dB(A)}\)?
To achieve Maximum Year-Round Insolation at a latitude of \(40^\circ\), what is the optimum tilt angle?
Calculate the mass of \(CO_2\) produced from the complete combustion of 44 kg of Propane (\(C_3H_8\)).
According to the “Combustion” table, what are the reaction products for the combustion of Sulfur to Sulfur Trioxide?
Determine the number of moles of Oxygen (\(O_2\)) required to completely combust 1 mole of Propane (\(C_3H_8\)).
Calculate the kinetic energy contained in a \(1,000\ \mathrm{kg}\) mass of air moving at a wind speed of \(10\ \mathrm{m/s}\).
Calculate the power delivered by water (\(P\)) in kilowatts (\(kW\)) of a hydroelectric turbine. The flow rate is \(Q = 5\ \mathrm{m^3/s}\), the net head is \(H = 20\ \mathrm{m}\).

Calculate the Sustainability Impact (SI) with the given values.
Given:
\(P = 1,000,000\ \text{persons}\)

\(GDP/P = \$50,000/\text{person-yr}\)

\(E/GDP = 0.005\ \mathrm{Btu/\$}\)

A civil engineering firm is submitting a proposal for a large municipal wastewater treatment plant. To make their proposal more attractive, the firm lists a renowned wastewater expert as a “Key Consultant” in their organizational chart. However, the firm has not actually contacted this expert or secured their agreement to work on the project. Is this action ethical according to the NCEES Model Rules?

choices.A: Yes, provided the firm fully intends to hire the expert if they win the contract.
choices.B: No, because it constitutes a misrepresentation of the firm’s professional qualifications and associations.
choices.C: Yes, because it is standard marketing practice to list potential team members in a proposal.
choices.D: No, unless the expert has previously worked with the firm on similar projects.

questions.question: Engineer A is competing with Engineer B for a lucrative contract. To improve his chances, Engineer A starts a rumor that Engineer B is currently under investigation for fraud, knowing this information is false. Is Engineer A’s conduct acceptable under the NCEES Model Rules?

choices.A: Yes, provided that Engineer A genuinely believes he is more qualified for the job than Engineer B.
choices.B: No, because licensees shall not maliciously or falsely attempt to injure the professional reputation of another licensee.
choices.C: Yes, because aggressive marketing strategies to highlight a competitor’s weaknesses are standard business practice.
choices.D: No, unless Engineer A submits a formal report to the state licensing board before spreading the rumor.

questions.question: An engineer is designing a chemical plant near a nature reserve. The design meets all federal emission standards. However, the engineer knows that even compliant emissions could harm a rare species of bird in the reserve over time. What should the engineer employ concern for:

choices.A: Compliance with the law only; exceeding standards is not required.
choices.B: Protection of ecosystems and environmental health.
choices.C: Maximizing shareholder value above all else.

questions.question: A professional engineer is hired by a land developer to design a subdivision. The construction contractor, who is building the subdivision, also asks the engineer to perform a structural inspection on the same project and offers to pay him for this additional service. How should the engineer respond to the contractor’s offer?

choices.A: Accept the offer immediately, as inspections are separate from design work.
choices.B: Decline the offer unless the circumstances are fully disclosed and agreed to in writing by all interested parties.
choices.C: Accept the offer but request that the payment be made in cash to avoid a conflict of interest trail.
choices.D: Decline the offer strictly because accepting payment from two parties on the same project is never allowed.

questions.question: An engineer is evaluating two different materials for a new beverage container. Material A is cheaper to manufacture but difficult to recycle. Material B is more expensive to manufacture but is 100% recyclable and uses less energy during disposal. To make an ethical decision based on sustainable principles, the engineer should perform a:

choices.A: Cost-Benefit Analysis focused solely on production costs.

questions.question: A company develops a new line of high-efficiency compressors and wants to protect the unique brand name and logo they have created for this product line to distinguish it from competitors. Which form of intellectual property protection is appropriate?
A company is granted a utility patent for a new hydraulic pump design in the United States. Assuming all maintenance fees are paid, how long does this patent protection generally last?

choices.A: 14 years from the date of issue.
choices.B: 17 years from the date of issue.
choices.C: 20 years from the date the application was filed.
choices.D: Indefinitely, as long as it is used in commerce.

questions.question: An engineer leaves Company A to work for a competitor, Company B. While at Company A, she developed a proprietary manufacturing process that gave Company A a significant economic advantage. This process was not patented but was kept confidential. Can she use this process at Company B?

choices.A: Yes, because it was not patented, it is public domain.
choices.B: Yes, because she developed it herself, she owns the intellectual property.
choices.C: No, because it is considered a Trade Secret of Company A.
choices.D: No, unless she changes at least 20% of the process steps.

questions.question: A mechanical engineer invents a new type of gear mechanism that significantly improves transmission efficiency. He also designs a unique, aesthetically pleasing casing for the gearbox that does not affect its function. To protect both the functional mechanism and the ornamental appearance, which types of patents should he apply for?

choices.A: Utility patent for the mechanism and Copyright for the casing.
choices.B: Utility patent for the mechanism and Design patent for the casing.
choices.C: Design patent for both the mechanism and the casing.
choices.D: Trade secret for the mechanism and Trademark for the casing.

questions.question: A Civil PE is the prime design professional for a commercial building project. The project includes structural, mechanical, and electrical components. The Civil PE signs and seals the civil and structural drawings, which he prepared. He also signs and seals the cover sheet for the entire set of plans, which includes the mechanical and electrical drawings prepared by other consultants. Is this action permissible?

choices.A: No, a licensee can never sign a document that contains work they did not personally prepare.
choices.B: Yes, provided that the mechanical and electrical drawings are each signed and sealed by their respective licensed professionals.
choices.C: Yes, because as the prime professional, he is automatically responsible for all technical aspects of the project.
choices.D: No, unless he possesses a license in all three disciplines (Civil, Mechanical, Electrical).

questions.question: John Doe graduated with a degree in civil engineering four years ago but has not yet passed the Principles and Practice of Engineering (PE) exam. He opens his own consulting business and prints business cards that read “John Doe, Civil Engineer.” In many jurisdictions based on the NCEES Model Law, is this permissible?

choices.A: Yes, because he has an accredited engineering degree.
choices.B: Yes, as long as he does not use the specific title “Professional Engineer” (PE).
choices.C: No, the use of the word “Engineer” in a business title offering services to the public is generally restricted to licensed individuals.
choices.D: No, unless he works under the direct supervision of a licensed PE in his own company.

questions.question: A civil engineer is designing a roadway through a sensitive wetland area. The client requests a route that is the most cost-effective but would require draining a significant portion of the wetland, potentially destroying the local ecosystem. According to the principle of sustainable development in engineering, the engineer should:

choices.A: Follow the client’s instructions as long as the design meets minimum highway safety standards.
choices.B: Design the cheapest route but donate personal funds to a local environmental charity.
choices.C: Advise the client on the long-term environmental impact and propose an alternative route that minimizes ecosystem damage, even if it costs more.
choices.D: Refuse the project immediately because building near wetlands is always unethical.

questions.question: A civil engineer is overseeing the construction of a high-rise building. During excavation, the engineer discovers that the soil conditions are significantly worse than indicated in the geotechnical report. Strengthening the foundation will cost an additional $2 million and delay the project by two months. The developer insists on proceeding with the original design to avoid financial losses, claiming the risk is “acceptable.” What is the engineer’s ethical obligation?

choices.A: Proceed with the original design but document the developer’s decision in writing to limit liability.
choices.B: Refuse to approve the work and notify the local building department if the developer persists.
choices.C: Suggest a compromise design that saves some money but still does not fully meet the safety code.
choices.D: Resign from the project immediately without notifying anyone to avoid conflict.

questions.question: A civil engineering firm wants to win a contract for a new city park. The firm’s principal learns that the mayor, who has the final say on the contract award, is running for re-election. The principal donates a large sum of money to the mayor’s campaign with the specific intent of influencing the contract decision. This action is:

choices.A: Ethical, as long as the donation is within the legal limit for campaign contributions.
choices.B: Ethical, provided the firm is actually the most qualified for the job.
choices.C: Unethical, because it constitutes a political contribution made with the intent to influence the award of a contract.
choices.D: Unethical, but only if the mayor explicitly asked for the money.

questions.question: Engineer A is retained by a client to review a design prepared by Engineer B. During the review, Engineer A identifies a calculation error that significantly reduces the load-bearing capacity of the structure, posing a safety risk. According to the NCEES Model Rules, what is Engineer A’s obligation regarding Engineer B?

choices.A: Correct the error silently and seal the new plans without involving Engineer B.
choices.B: Make a reasonable effort to inform Engineer B of the error, unless legally prohibited.
choices.C: Report Engineer B immediately to the state board for incompetence before notifying the client.
choices.D: Inform the client but strictly avoid contacting Engineer B to prevent conflict.

questions.question: A licensed Professional Engineer is convicted of tax evasion, a felony charge unrelated to his engineering practice. The state licensing board initiates disciplinary action to revoke his license. The engineer argues that his license cannot be revoked because the crime did not involve engineering competence or safety. Is the board’s action justified?

choices.A: No, the board can only discipline licensees for negligence in engineering practice.
choices.B: No, personal financial crimes are outside the board’s jurisdiction.
choices.C: Yes, conviction of any felony is grounds for disciplinary action, regardless of its relation to engineering.
choices.D: Yes, but only if the tax evasion occurred while managing a client’s funds.

questions.question: A Professional Engineer is hired by a large chemical company to attend a town hall meeting and argue against a proposed environmental regulation that would increase the company’s costs. The engineer introduces himself as a “concerned expert citizen” but does not reveal that he is being paid by the chemical company to speak. According to the NCEES Model Rules, is this acceptable?

choices.A: Yes, because he is expressing his honest professional opinion based on facts.
choices.B: Yes, as long as he does not lie about the technical data.
choices.C: No, he must explicitly identify the interested party on whose behalf he is speaking.
choices.D: No, engineers are prohibited from speaking at political town hall meetings.

questions.question: Licensee A gains knowledge that Licensee B has falsified data in a geotechnical report submitted for a public school project. Licensee A knows this violation could compromise the building’s foundation. According to the NCEES Model Rules, what is Licensee A’s obligation?

choices.A: Confront Licensee B privately and ask him to fix the report.
choices.B: Ignore the situation to avoid damaging a professional colleague’s reputation.
choices.C: Report the violation to the licensure board and cooperate with their investigation.
choices.D: Anonymous leak the information to the school district’s principal.

questions.question: A Professional Engineer is asked by his supervisor to sign and seal a set of design drawings prepared by a junior engineer in a different branch office. The PE did not supervise the design process, did not review the calculations, and has not visited the site, but he trusts the junior engineer’s competence. Which of the following statements is true regarding the PE’s authority to seal these documents?

choices.A: He may seal them because the junior engineer works for the same company.
choices.B: He may seal them if he conducts a quick spot-check of the final drawings.
choices.C: He may not seal them because they were not prepared under his responsible charge.
choices.D: He may seal them provided the company assumes full liability insurance.

questions.question: Engineer X recently left Firm A to join Firm B. Firm B is now bidding on a project for a client that Engineer X worked with while at Firm A. Firm B asks Engineer X to share specific cost data and design details from the previous project to help them prepare a competitive bid. The data is not public record. How should Engineer X respond?

choices.A: Share the data since he was the original author of the design documents.
choices.B: Refuse to share the data unless he obtains prior consent from Firm A and the client.
choices.C: Share the data but remove the client’s name to maintain anonymity.
choices.D: Refuse to share the data unless the new project is identical to the old one.

questions.question: An engineer is part of a selection committee to award a construction contract for a new highway bridge. Upon reviewing the list of bidders, the engineer realizes that one of the construction firms is owned by his first cousin. The engineer believes he can remain impartial. According to the NCEES Model Rules, what must the engineer do?

choices.A: Recuse himself from the committee without explanation to maintain family privacy.
choices.B: Remain on the committee but vote against his cousin’s firm to prove impartiality.
choices.C: Disclose the relationship to his employer and the committee members immediately.
choices.D: Keep the relationship confidential since a cousin is not considered an immediate family member.

questions.question: A Professional Engineer (PE) licensed in Civil Engineering is asked by his firm to seal a set of electrical design drawings because the staff Electrical PE is currently hospitalized and the project deadline is today. The Civil PE has taken a few basic electrical courses in college but has no significant work experience in power systems. According to the NCEES Model Rules, what is the engineer’s most appropriate course of action?

choices.A: Seal the drawings to ensure the firm meets the deadline, provided the Electrical PE reviews them later.
choices.B: Refuse to seal the drawings because he lacks competence in the specific technical field.
choices.C: Seal the drawings but include a disclaimer stating that his expertise is primarily in Civil Engineering.
choices.D: Review the drawings for general compliance and then seal them under his responsible charge.

questions.question: Engineer B is responsible for selecting a vendor for a large municipal pump station project. One of the competing vendors, Vendor X, invites Engineer B to an all-expenses-paid “technical seminar” at a luxury golf resort in Hawaii. The seminar takes up two hours of the three-day trip. According to the NCEES Model Rules, Engineer B should:

choices.A: Accept the invitation provided the trip is disclosed to his employer.
choices.B: Accept the invitation but pay for his own airfare to show partial independence.
choices.C: Decline the invitation, as it constitutes a gratuity that could influence his judgment.
choices.D: Accept the invitation only if Vendor X is the lowest bidder.

questions.question: An engineer is hired as an expert witness by a plaintiff in a structural failure lawsuit. During the investigation, the engineer finds a report that suggests the plaintiff’s own lack of maintenance contributed significantly to the failure. This information hurts the client’s case. According to the NCEES Model Rules, the engineer must:

choices.A: Exclude this information from the testimony to protect the client’s interest.
choices.B: Include all relevant and pertinent information in an objective and truthful manner.
choices.C: Withdraw from the case to avoid a conflict of interest.
choices.D: Classify the report as a “trade secret” to prevent it from being entered into evidence.

questions.question: Engineer A works for a manufacturing company. She discovers that a chemical discharge valve is malfunctioning and releasing a level of toxins slightly above the EPA limit into a local river. She reports this to her plant manager, who tells her that fixing it would require a costly shutdown and that she should “let it go for now” since the excess is minimal. What is Engineer A’s obligation?

choices.A: Document the conversation with the manager in a personal log and take no further action.
choices.B: Immediately contact the local news media to expose the violation to the public.
choices.C: Notify the appropriate regulatory authority since the manager has refused to correct the safety hazard.
choices.D: Resign from the company to avoid legal liability.

questions.question: An engineer is retained by a developer to design a retaining wall for a residential community. During the design phase, the engineer discovers that the soil conditions on-site are unstable and require a more expensive reinforcement system than originally budgeted. The developer insists on using the cheaper, original design to stay within budget and assures the engineer that they will sign a liability waiver releasing the engineer from any future responsibility. How should the engineer respond?

choices.A: Proceed with the cheaper design after the waiver is signed and notarized to protect against lawsuits.
choices.B: Withdraw from the project immediately and maintain confidentiality regarding the soil conditions.
choices.C: Refuse to seal the plans and advise the developer that the design must be modified to ensure public safety.
choices.D: Seal the plans but attach a memo to the building department outlining the potential risks.

questions.question: A light metal ring rests on the surface of water with a total contact length of \(0.12\ \text{m}\). A horizontal force of \(3.6\times 10^{-3}\ \text{N}\) is required to slide the ring free from the water surface. Determine the surface tension of the water (N/m).

A small flat plate with a surface area of \(0.01\ \text{m}^2\) lies on a fluid layer that is \(0.002\ \text{m}\) thick. The plate is moved horizontally at a constant velocity of \(0.1\ \text{m/s}\). If a horizontal force of \(1.0\ \text{N}\) is required to maintain this motion, determine the dynamic viscosity of the fluid (in Ns/m\(^2\)).

A small flat plate with a surface area of \( 0.01 \, \text{m}^2 \) lies on a fluid layer that is \( 0.002 \, \text{m} \) thick. If the plate is moved horizontally at a constant velocity of \( 0.1 \, \text{m/s} \), and the dynamic viscosity of the fluid is \( 2 \, \text{Ns/m}^2 \), determine the horizontal force required to maintain this motion.

A homogeneous mixture is created by combining \( 18 \, \mathrm{kg} \) of a fluid with a density of \( 920 \, \mathrm{kg/m^3} \) and \( 6 \, \mathrm{kg} \) of water. Assuming the volumes are additive, the specific volume of the resulting mixture is most nearly:

A wooden block with square cross-section \(0.5\ \text{m} \times 0.5\ \text{m}\) and length \(1.0\ \text{m}\) floats in fresh water with its long axis horizontal. The wood has specific gravity \(SG = 0.60\). Assuming water with \(\gamma_w = 9.81\ \text{kN/m}^3\), determine the submerged depth of the block when the block is in static equilibrium.

A circular drainage conduit has an inside diameter of \(4\ \text{m}\) and is half full of water（Shown as below).
Assuming water with specific weight \(\gamma = 9.81\ \text{kN/m}^3\), determine the magnitude of the resultant force that the water exerts on the curved wall segment \(AB\).

A solid rectangular block is fully submerged in fresh water. The block dimensions are \(1.2\ \text{m} \times 0.8\ \text{m} \times 0.5\ \text{m}\). Assuming water with specific weight \(\gamma = 9.81\ \text{kN/m}^3\), determine the magnitude of the buoyant force acting on the block.

A rectangular barge has a uniform cross-section \(6\ \text{m}\) long (in plan) and \(2\ \text{m}\) wide. When floating in calm water, the barge is such that \(0.6\ \text{m}\) of its depth is submerged below the water surface. The submerged cross-section is therefore a \(6\ \text{m} \times 0.6\ \text{m}\) rectangle. Determine the vertical distance from the water surface to the center of buoyancy.
references:

Therefore:

\]

the resultant hydrostatic force \(F_R\) on the hatch, and

the depth \(h_{CP}\) of the center of pressure below the surface.

the resultant hydrostatic force on the submerged portion, and

the depth \(h_{CP}\) of the center of pressure below the water surface.

the resultant hydrostatic force \(F_R\) on the gate, and

the vertical distance \(h_{CP}\) from the water surface to the center of pressure.

questions.question: An incompressible fluid flows steadily through a 6-inch diameter pipe at a velocity of 12 m/s. It then enters a narrower 4-inch diameter pipe. Estimate the velocity in the new pipe.

questions.question: A pipe carrying an incompressible fluid has a diameter of \( 120\,\mathrm{mm} \) at point 1 and a diameter of \( 60\,\mathrm{mm} \) at point 2. The velocity of the fluid at point 1 is \( 0.25\,\mathrm{m/s} \). What is most nearly the flow velocity at point 2?
tags: Principles Of One Dimensional Fluid Flow

questions.question: A Newtonian fluid flows through a circular tube of radius \(0.05\ \text{m}\). The wall shear stress is measured to be \(\tau_w = 12\ \text{Pa}\). Determine the shear stress at a radial position \(r = 0.02\ \text{m}\).

A Newtonian fluid flows steadily between two large parallel plates that are \(8\ \text{mm}\) apart. The flow is laminar. The average velocity \(\bar v \) in the gap is \( 0.40\ \text{m/s}\). Determine the local velocity at a point that is \(2\ \text{mm}\) from the center plane.

A fluid flows at a velocity of \(0.6\ \text{m/s}\) through a \(0.08\ \text{m}\) diameter pipe. The kinematic viscosity of the fluid is \(1.5\times10^{-5}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}\). Determine the most likely flow regime.

A Newtonian fluid flows through a circular tube of radius \(0.04\ \text{m}\). The flow is steady and laminar. The average velocity in the tube is measured to be \(0.5\ \text{m/s}\). Using the velocity distribution for laminar flow in circular tubes, determine the local fluid velocity at a radial position \(r = 0.02\ \text{m}\).
references:
FE Reference Handbook 10.5, P182:

Fluid Mechanics – Fluid Flow Characterization

references:

questions.question: Oil flows through an old cast-iron pipeline. The Reynolds number of the flow is \( Re = 1.8\times10^{6} \), and the relative roughness of the pipe is \( \epsilon/D = 0.015 \). Using the Moody chart, estimate the Darcy–Weisbach friction factor \( f \) for this fully turbulent flow.
A noncircular air duct is flowing full. The cross-sectional flow area is \(A = 1.8\ \text{ft}^2\), and the wetted perimeter is \(P = 4.5\ \text{ft}\). Determine the hydraulic diameter of the duct.
A pipe carries water with a Reynolds number of \( Re = 400{,}000 \). The relative roughness of the pipe is \( \epsilon/D = 0.006 \). Determine the Darcy–Weisbach friction factor \( f \).

A fluid is flowing at a velocity of \(2.0\ \text{m/s}\) in a circular conduit with an inside diameter of \(0.030\ \text{m}\). The length of the conduit is \(60\ \text{m}\). The Moody friction factor for the conduit is \(f = 0.020\). Assuming steady, incompressible flow of water, determine the head loss due to friction in the conduit.

Water flows steadily through a horizontal steel pipeline with an inside diameter of \(0.25\ \text{m}\) and a length of \(120\ \text{m}\). The average velocity of flow is \(1.8\ \text{m/s}\). The Darcy–Weisbach friction factor for the pipe is \(f = 0.018\). Neglecting minor losses, determine the head loss due to friction

in the pipe.

A noncircular storm sewer is flowing full. At a given cross section, the flow area is \(A = 2.4\ \text{m}^2\), and the wetted perimeter is \(P = 6.0\ \text{m}\). Determine the hydraulic radius of the flow at that section.

As the fluid traverses the shock, kinetic energy is violently converted to pressure. Use the normal shock relationships to determine the static pressure ratio (\( P_2 / P_1 \)) across the wave.

What is most nearly the required area ratio (\( A_e / A^* \)) of the exit area to the throat area?

A pitot-static tube is utilized to measure the airspeed of a high-performance aircraft operating in the transonic regime. The aircraft is flying at a Mach number of \( Ma = 0.85 \) through air (\( k = 1.4 \)). The static pressure port on the instrument reads the ambient pressure \( P = 40 \ \mathrm{kPa} \). Assuming the deceleration of the air at the pitot tube’s stagnation point is an isentropic process, what is most nearly the ratio of the stagnation pressure to the static pressure (\( P_0 / P \))?

A stagnation temperature probe is mounted on the nose of a supersonic military aircraft. The aircraft is traveling at a Mach number of \( Ma = 2.0 \) through ambient air (\( k = 1.4 \)) that has a static absolute temperature of \( T = 220 \ \mathrm{K} \) and a static pressure of \( P = 26 \ \mathrm{kPa} \). Assuming the air is brought to rest isentropically at the tip of the probe, what is most nearly the stagnation temperature (\( T_0 \)) recorded by the sensor?
Ma = 2.0, T = 220 K

A commercial jetliner is cruising at an altitude of \( 10,000 \ \mathrm{m} \). The aircraft’s true airspeed is determined to be \( V = 250 \ \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s} \). At this altitude, the ambient static temperature of the air (\( k = 1.4, \ R = 287 \ \mathrm{J}/(\mathrm{kg}\cdot\mathrm{K}) \)) is measured at \( -40^\circ\mathrm{C} \). What is most nearly the Mach number (\( Ma \)) of the aircraft?

A supersonic wind tunnel is being prepared for aerodynamic testing of a new airfoil profile. The working fluid is dry air, which behaves as an ideal gas with a specific heat ratio of \( k = 1.4 \) and a specific gas constant of \( R = 287 \ \mathrm{J}/(\mathrm{kg}\cdot\mathrm{K}) \). Sensors in the test section record a static absolute pressure of \( P = 45 \ \mathrm{kPa} \) and a static temperature of \( T = -20^\circ\mathrm{C} \). What is most nearly the local speed of sound (\( c \)) in the test section?

As part of an industrial cogeneration power plant, hot combustion gases (modeled as ideal air with a constant specific heat of \( c_p = 1000 \ \mathrm{J}/(\mathrm{kg}\cdot\mathrm{K}) \)) enter an axial-flow gas turbine. Sensors record a steady mass flow rate of \( \dot{m} = 2.5 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{s} \) with an absolute inlet temperature of \( T_i = 800 \ \mathrm{K} \). After expanding through the turbine stages, the exhaust gas temperature drops significantly to \( T_e = 400 \ \mathrm{K} \). Assuming the expansion process is ideal and adiabatic with negligible changes in kinetic and potential energy, what is most nearly the theoretical mechanical power (\( \dot{W}_{turb} \)) produced at the turbine shaft?

A typical backward curved fan is used in an HVAC duct system. The fan generates a pressure rise of \( \Delta P = 600 \ \mathrm{Pa} \) (\( \mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}^2 \)) while moving a volumetric flow rate of \( Q = 5.0 \ \mathrm{m}^3/\mathrm{s} \). If the fan efficiency is \( \eta_f = 0.75 \), what is the required fan power (\( \dot{W} \))?

Air enters an ideal isothermal compressor (\( \eta_c = 1.0 \)) at a temperature of \( T_i = 293 \ \mathrm{K} \) and a mass flow rate of \( \dot{m} = 0.24 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{s} \). The pressure ratio from exit to inlet is \( P_e / P_i = 6.0 \). The universal gas constant is \( \bar{R} = 8314 \ \mathrm{J}/(\mathrm{kmol}\cdot\mathrm{K}) \) and the molecular weight of air is \( M = 29 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{kmol} \). Calculate the power consumed (\( |\dot{W}_{comp}| \)).

A primary air compressor in a manufacturing plant’s pneumatic system draws in ambient air (\( k = 1.4 \)) at an absolute inlet pressure of \( P_i = 100 \ \mathrm{kPa} \). Sensors indicate that the mass flow rate entering the unit is \( \dot{m} = 0.24 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{s} \) with a corresponding inlet density of \( \rho_i = 1.2 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}^3 \). The air is then compressed and discharged into a receiver tank at a pressure of \( P_e = 600 \ \mathrm{kPa} \). Assuming the compression process is adiabatic and the machine operates at an ideal isentropic efficiency of \( \eta_c = 1.0 \), what is most nearly the mechanical power (\( |\dot{W}_{comp}| \)) required to drive this compressor?

An industrial cooling system is currently equipped with an oversized centrifugal pump featuring a \( D_1 = 10.0 \ \mathrm{in.} \) diameter impeller. Under baseline continuous operation, the pump draws a brake power of \( \dot{W}_1 = 15 \ \mathrm{hp} \). To optimize system efficiency and eliminate excessive throttling valve losses, plant engineers decide to physically trim the pump’s impeller down to a new diameter of \( D_2 = 9.0 \ \mathrm{in.} \). Assuming the pump continues to be driven at the exact same rotational speed (\( N_2 = N_1 \)) and handles the same fluid (\( \rho_2 = \rho_1 \)), what is most nearly the expected new power requirement (\( \dot{W}_2 \)) ?

A municipal water treatment plant needs to increase its daily throughput. An existing centrifugal pump currently operates at a rotational speed of \( N_1 = 1750 \ \mathrm{rpm} \) and delivers a baseline flow rate of \( Q_1 = 400 \ \mathrm{GPM} \). To meet the new capacity demands, engineers install a Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) to increase the pump’s motor speed to \( N_2 = 2100 \ \mathrm{rpm} \). Assuming the impeller diameter (\( D \)) remains unchanged and the system curve is compatible, what is most nearly the new volumetric flow rate (\( Q_2 \)) delivered by the pump?

A pump system transports liquid fertilizer (\( \rho = 1150 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}^3 \)). The system requires a flow rate of \( Q = 0.2 \ \mathrm{m}^3/\mathrm{s} \) and a total head increase of \( H = 30 \ \mathrm{m} \). The pump has an efficiency of \( \eta_{pump} = 0.78 \), and the electric motor has an efficiency of \( \eta_{motor} = 0.92 \). Following the sequential power definitions in the NCEES Handbook, what is most nearly the required purchased electrical power (\( \dot{W}_{purchased} \))?

A centrifugal pump operates continuously to extract water (\( \rho = 1000 \ \mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}^3 \)). It delivers a steady volumetric flow rate of \( Q = 0.05 \ \mathrm{m}^3/\mathrm{s} \) against a total head increase of \( H = 45 \ \mathrm{m} \). What is most nearly the ideal fluid power (\( \dot{W}_{fluid} \)) imparted to the water?

An open basin supplies water to a pump. The atmospheric pressure is \( P_{atm} = 14.7 \ \mathrm{psia} \) and the fluid’s specific weight is \( \gamma = 62.4 \ \mathrm{lbf}/\mathrm{ft}^3 \). The fluid vapor pressure is \( P_{vapor} = 0.26 \ \mathrm{psia} \). The pump is installed with a suction lift, meaning the water surface is \( 8.0 \ \mathrm{ft} \) below the pump impeller centerline. Total friction losses in the suction line are \( \Sigma h_L = 2.5 \ \mathrm{ft} \). What is most nearly the Net Positive Suction Head Available (\( NPSH_A \))?

If the physical area of the orifice is \( A_0 = 0.5 \ \mathrm{m}^2 \) and the calibrated coefficient of discharge is \( C = 0.65 \), what is most nearly the steady volumetric flow rate (\( Q \)) passing through the submerged orifice?

questions.question: A 2 kg steel block (\(c = 500\ \text{J}/(\text{kg}\cdot\text{K})\)) is initially at \(400^\circ\text{C}\). It is quenched in an oil bath at \(50^\circ\text{C}\). Assuming the lumped capacitance model is valid, what is the total amount of heat energy (\(Q_{total}\)) transferred from the block to the oil when the block reaches thermal equilibrium?
tags: Transient Conduction Using The Lumped Capacitance Model

questions.question: A copper pin fin (\(k = 400\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\)) has a diameter of \(2\ \text{mm}\) and a length of \(20\ \text{mm}\). The base temperature is \(100^\circ\text{C}\) and the ambient air is \(20^\circ\text{C}\) with \(h = 25\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Using the adiabatic tip assumption with corrected length, calculate the heat loss from the fin.

A cylindrical pin fin made of aluminum (\(k = 200\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\)) has a diameter of \(D = 5\ \text{mm}\). The convection heat transfer coefficient is \(h = 40\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Calculate the fin parameter \(m\).

A steam pipe is covered with insulation. The pipe can be modeled as a cylindrical wall with an inner radius \(r_1 = 0.05\ \text{m}\), an outer radius \(r_2 = 0.10\ \text{m}\), and a length \(L = 5\ \text{m}\). The thermal conductivity of the insulation is \(k = 0.5\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\). The inner surface temperature is \(150^\circ\text{C}\) and the outer surface temperature is \(50^\circ\text{C}\). Calculate the rate of heat loss from the pipe.

Two aluminum plates (\(k = 240\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\)), each \(2\ \text{cm}\) thick, are bolted together. The contact pressure results in a thermal contact conductance of \(h_c = 10,000\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\) at the interface. The outer surface of the first plate is at \(400^\circ\text{C}\), and the outer surface of the second plate is at \(300^\circ\text{C}\). Calculate the rate of heat transfer per unit area (heat flux) through the plates.

A “pin fin” (cylindrical cross-section) has a diameter \(D = 10\ \text{mm}\) and a length \(L = 40\ \text{mm}\). When performing heat transfer calculations using the corrected length method described in the NCEES Handbook, what is the value of \(L_c\)?

A rectangular aluminum fin (\(k = 200\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\)) has a thickness of \(2\ \text{mm}\), a length of \(50\ \text{mm}\), and a width of \(1\ \text{m}\). The base temperature is \(150^\circ\text{C}\) and the fluid temperature is \(50^\circ\text{C}\) with \(h = 50\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Assuming  negligible heat transfer from tip, calculate the heat transfer rate from the fin.

A large plane wall of thickness \(2L = 0.1\ \text{m}\) is initially at a uniform temperature of \(T_i = 300^\circ\text{C}\). It is suddenly exposed to convection on both sides with \(T_\infty = 30^\circ\text{C}\) and \(h = 400\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). The properties of the wall are \(k = 20\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\) and \(\alpha = 1 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}\). Calculate the temperature at the midplane (\(T_0\)) after \(125\ \text{s}\).
tags: Approximate Solution For Solid With Sudden Convection

questions.question: Which of the following conditions must be satisfied for the lumped capacitance method to be considered valid for transient heat transfer analysis?
tags: Transient Conduction Using The Lumped Capacitance Model

questions.question: A small copper ball (\(\rho = 8900\ \text{kg/m}^3\), \(c_p = 380\ \text{J}/(\text{kg}\cdot\text{K})\)) with a diameter of \(10\ \text{mm}\) is initially at \(250^\circ\text{C}\). It is dropped into an oil bath at \(30^\circ\text{C}\) with \(h = 40\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Assuming the lumped capacitance model is valid, calculate the time constant (\(\tau\)) for this cooling process.
tags: Transient Conduction Using The Lumped Capacitance Model

questions.question: A solid steel sphere with a diameter of \(12\ \text{mm}\) is cooling in air. The thermal conductivity of steel is \(k = 40\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\) and the convection coefficient is \(h = 20\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Calculate the Biot number (\(Bi\)) for this process.
tags: Transient Conduction Using The Lumped Capacitance Model

questions.question: A steam pipe with an outer diameter of \(60\ \text{mm}\) is covered with insulation having a thermal conductivity \(k = 0.15\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\). The convection heat transfer coefficient to the surrounding air is \(h = 10\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). If the thickness of the insulation is increased from \(5\ \text{mm}\) to \(10\ \text{mm}\), how is the heat transfer rate affected?

A plane wall with a thickness of \(L = 0.1\ \text{m}\) and thermal conductivity \(k = 1.0\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\) separates two fluids. Fluid 1 is at \(T_{\infty,1} = 200^\circ\text{C}\) with \(h_1 = 50\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Fluid 2 is at \(T_{\infty,2} = 50^\circ\text{C}\) with \(h_2 = 20\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Calculate the total thermal resistance per unit area (\(R_{total}\)) for this system.

A composite wall is composed of three layers. Layer 1 has \(R_1 = 0.5\ \text{K/W}\), Layer 2 has \(R_2 = 1.0\ \text{K/W}\), and Layer 3 has \(R_3 = 0.5\ \text{K/W}\). If the temperature of the outer surface of Layer 1 is \(400^\circ\text{C}\) and the outer surface of Layer 3 is \(100^\circ\text{C}\), what is the temperature drop across Layer 2?

An insulating material is needed to limit heat loss through a wall to \(200\ \text{W/m}^2\). The temperature difference across the insulation is \(50^\circ\text{C}\). If the thermal conductivity of the material is \(k = 0.04\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\), what is the minimum required thickness?

Heat is flowing through a large plate with a thickness of \(L = 50\ \text{mm}\). The thermal conductivity is \(k = 15\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\). The rate of heat transfer per unit area is measured to be \(\frac{\dot{Q} }{A} = 6000\ \text{W/m}^2\). If the hotter surface is at \(120^\circ\text{C}\), what is the temperature of the colder surface?

A plane wall (\(k = 0.8\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\)) is \(20\ \text{cm}\) thick. The inner surface is kept at \(150^\circ\text{C}\). The outer surface is exposed to air at \(20^\circ\text{C}\) with a convection coefficient of \(h = 10\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Calculate the temperature of the outer surface (\(T_s\)).

A steel pipe (\(k = 50\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\)) has an inner radius of \(2\ \text{cm}\) and an outer radius of \(2.5\ \text{cm}\). It is covered with a layer of insulation (\(k = 0.1\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\)) that is \(1\ \text{cm}\) thick. The pipe is \(10\ \text{m}\) long. If the inner surface temperature of the pipe is \(200^\circ\text{C}\) and the outer surface temperature of the insulation is \(30^\circ\text{C}\), what is the total heat loss rate?

A hot water pipe (\(r_{outer} = 2\ \text{cm}\)) is covered with insulation (\(k = 0.1\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\)) having an outer radius of \(4\ \text{cm}\). The length is \(10\ \text{m}\). The convection heat transfer coefficient on the outer surface is \(h = 10\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Calculate the total thermal resistance (\(R_{total}\)) of the insulation and convection.

A copper wire has a radius of \(r_{wire} = 3\ \text{mm}\). It is covered with insulation that has a critical radius of \(r_{cr} = 10\ \text{mm}\). If the thickness of the insulation is increased such that the outer radius goes from \(5\ \text{mm}\) to \(7\ \text{mm}\), what happens to the heat transfer rate?

choices.B: The heat transfer rate remains constant.

questions.question: An electric wire is being covered with plastic insulation having a thermal conductivity of \(k_{ins} = 0.15\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\). The wire is exposed to air with a convection heat transfer coefficient of \(h_\infty = 15\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Calculate the critical radius of insulation (\(r_{cr}\)).

A steam pipe is covered with a layer of insulation. The insulation has an inner radius of \(r_1 = 5\ \text{cm}\), an outer radius of \(r_2 = 10\ \text{cm}\), and a thermal conductivity of \(k = 0.05\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\). The length of the pipe is \(L = 1\ \text{m}\). What is the thermal resistance of this insulation layer?

A steel pipe (\(k = 50\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\)) with a length of \(50\ \text{m}\) has an inner radius \(r_1 = 0.05\ \text{m}\) and an outer radius \(r_2 = 0.06\ \text{m}\). The inner surface temperature is \(150^\circ\text{C}\) and the outer surface temperature is \(140^\circ\text{C}\). Calculate the rate of heat loss \(\dot{Q}\) through the pipe wall.

A window glass with a surface area of \(A = 1.5\ \text{m}^2\) is exposed to outside air. The convection heat transfer coefficient is \(h = 25\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). What is the thermal resistance due to convection on the outside surface?

Consider a composite wall with two layers, A and B, in series. The total heat transfer rate is determined to be \(\dot{Q} = 1167\ \text{W}\). The inner layer (A) has a thermal resistance of \(R_A = 0.1\ \text{K/W}\) and the inner surface temperature is \(T_1 = 1000\ \text{K}\). What is the temperature at the interface between Layer A and Layer B?

A furnace wall consists of two layers. Layer A (Firebrick) has \(R_A = 0.1\ \text{K/W}\). Layer B (Insulating brick) has \(R_B = 0.5\ \text{K/W}\). The inner surface temperature is \(1000\ \text{K}\) and the outer surface temperature is \(300\ \text{K}\). What is the rate of heat loss \(\dot{Q}\) through the composite wall?

A large concrete wall has a thickness of \(L = 0.2\ \text{m}\) and a thermal conductivity of \(k = 1.2\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\). The temperature on one surface of the wall is measured to be \(25^\circ\text{C}\), and the temperature on the other surface is \(5^\circ\text{C}\). Calculate the rate of heat transfer through the wall per unit surface area.

Water boils at 1 atm. To determine the boundary between transition boiling and film boiling, the minimum heat flux (Leidenfrost point) must be calculated. The following properties are given:
Liquid density, \(\rho_l = 958\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}\)

Vapor density, \(\rho_v = 0.597\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}\)

Surface tension, \(\sigma = 0.0589\ \mathrm{N/m}\)

Enthalpy of vaporization, \(h_{fg} = 2,257\ \mathrm{kJ/kg}\)

Acceleration of gravity, \(g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}\)
Calculate the minimum heat flux \(\dot{q}_{min}\).

A heater with a specific geometry is used to boil water at 1 atm. The following properties are given:
Characteristic length, \(L = 0.05\ \mathrm{m}\)

Liquid density, \(\rho_l = 958\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}\)

Vapor density, \(\rho_v = 0.6\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}\)

Surface tension, \(\sigma = 0.059\ \mathrm{N/m}\)
Calculate the dimensionless characteristic length \(L^*\).

Saturated liquid boils on the outer surface of a horizontal cylinder heater. The following information is provided:
Heater geometry: Horizontal cylinder

Dimensionless characteristic length, \(L^* = 5.0\)
Determine the value of the constant \(C_{cr}\) for this setup.

Water at 1 atm (\(T_{sat} = 100^\circ \mathrm{C}\)) is heated by a submerged horizontal surface maintained at \(T_s = 112^\circ \mathrm{C}\). Based on the “Typical boiling curve for water at one atmosphere” provided in the NCEES FE Reference Handbook 10.5, identify the boiling regime occurring at the surface.
A horizontal cylinder loses heat to the surrounding air. The Rayleigh number based on the diameter is \(Ra_D = 5 \times 10^5\). Calculate the average Nusselt number \(\overline{Nu}_D\) .

Estimate the Critical Heat Flux (CHF) for a liquid boiling on a large horizontal heater. The constants are \(C_{cr} = 0.15\), \(h_{fg} = 2257\ \mathrm{kJ/kg}\), \(\rho_v = 0.59\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}\), \(\sigma = 0.059\ \mathrm{N/m}\), \(g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}\), and \(\rho_l = 958\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}\).
Air flows over a sphere with a Reynolds number \(Re_D = 10,000\) and Prandtl number \(Pr = 0.7\). Calculate the Nusselt number \( \overline{Nu_D} \).

A long horizontal cylinder loses heat via natural convection. The Rayleigh number based on diameter is \(Ra_D = 10^6\). Calculate the average Nusselt number \(\overline{Nu}_D\) using the coefficients provided in the NCEES FE Reference Handbook 10.5.
A vertical flat plate is subjected to natural convection in air. The Rayleigh number based on length is \(Ra_L = 5 \times 10^5\). Calculate the average Nusselt number \(\overline{Nu}_L\).
Liquid sodium flows through a circular tube maintained at a constant wall temperature. The flow has \(Re_D Pr = 400\). Calculate the Nusselt number \(Nu_D\).
Air flows over a sphere (\(Re_D = 10,000, Pr = 0.7\)). Calculate \(Nu_D\).
Water flows in an annulus with an inner diameter \(D_i = 30\ \mathrm{mm}\) and an outer diameter \(D_o = 50\ \mathrm{mm}\). Calculate the hydraulic diameter \(D_h\).

Oil (\(Pr = 500\)) flows in a laminar state (\(Re_D = 100\)) in a tube with \(D/L = 0.02\). The viscosity ratio term \( \mu_b  / \mu_s = 1.0 \). Calculate \(Nu_D\) using the Sieder-Tate correlation for the combined entry length.

A fluid flows through a \(2\ \text{cm}\) diameter tube. The flow is turbulent (\(Re_D = 20,000\), \(Pr = 10\)). The viscosity correction factor \((\mu_b/\mu_s)^{0.14}\) is 1.10. The thermal conductivity of the fluid is \(k = 0.6\ \mathrm{W/(m\cdot K)}\). Calculate the convection heat transfer coefficient \(h\) using the Sieder-Tate correlation.
Hot oil (\(Pr = 50\)) is cooled in a tube (\(Re_D = 25,000\)). The viscosity ratio is \(\mu_b / \mu_s = 0.25\). Calculate \(Nu_D\) using the Sieder-Tate equation.
Engine oil flows through a heated tube (\(Re_D = 12,000\), \(Pr = 80\)). The viscosity ratio is \(\mu_b/\mu_s = 0.48/0.15 = 3.2\). Calculate \(Nu_D\) using the Sieder-Tate correlation.
Liquid mercury (\(Pr = 0.025\)) flows through a tube with a Reynolds number \(Re_D = 20,000\). The tube wall is maintained at a constant surface temperature. Determine the Nusselt number (\(Nu_D\)).

Air flows through a rectangular duct with dimensions \(0.2\ \text{m}\) by \(0.4\ \text{m}\). To use standard correlations for circular tubes, the characteristic length (hydraulic diameter, \(D_h\)) must be calculated. What is the value of \(D_h\)?
Hot oil (\(Pr = 50\)) flows through a cooling tube with \(Re_D = 20,000\). The oil is being cooled by the tube walls. Calculate the Nusselt number (\(Nu_D\)) using the Dittus-Boelter correlation.

Water (\(Pr = 5.0\)) flows through a tube with a Reynolds number \(Re_D = 40,000\). The water enters at \(20^\circ\text{C}\) and the tube wall is heated to \(60^\circ\text{C}\). Using the Dittus-Boelter equation, calculate the Nusselt number (\(Nu_D\)).

Water flows through a small diameter tube with \(Re_D = 1800\). The tube wall is subjected to a uniform surface heat flux. Calculate the Nusselt number (\(Nu_D\)) assuming the flow is fully developed.

Engine oil flows through a circular tube of diameter \(D = 0.02\ \text{m}\). The Reynolds number is calculated to be \(Re_D = 1500\). The tube surface is maintained at a uniform constant temperature. Determine the Nusselt number (\(Nu_D\)) for fully developed conditions.

Air flows in cross flow over a cylinder of diameter \(D\). The Reynolds number is calculated to be \(Re_D = 20,000\). The Prandtl number is \(0.7\). Determine the Nusselt number (\(\overline{Nu}_D\)).

Air flows parallel over a smooth flat plate of length \(L = 0.5\ \text{m}\) with a velocity of \(5\ \text{m/s}\). The density of the air is \(\rho = 1.2\ \text{kg/m}^3\) and the dynamic viscosity is \(\mu = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{kg}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{s})\). The Prandtl number is \(Pr = 0.7\). Calculate the average Nusselt number (\(\overline{Nu}_L\)) for the entire plate.

A plane wall (\(k = 0.8\ \text{W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})\)) is \(20\ \text{cm}\) thick. The inner surface is kept at \(150^\circ\text{C}\). The outer surface is exposed to air at \(20^\circ\text{C}\) with a convection coefficient of \(h = 10\ \text{W}/(\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K})\). Calculate the temperature of the outer surface (\(T_s\)).

Two black surfaces, \(A_1 = 1.5\ \mathrm{m^2}\) and \(A_2 = 1.5\ \mathrm{m^2}\), face each other in a vacuum. The view factor from Surface 1 to Surface 2 is \(F_{12} = 0.4\). Surface 1 is at \(T_1 = 1,000\ \mathrm{K}\) and Surface 2 is at \(T_2 = 500\ \mathrm{K}\). Calculate the net radiation heat exchange between the two black bodies.
tags: Net Energy Exchange By Radiation Between Two Bodies

questions.question:
An electronic component is cooled by radiation to the surrounding casing. The following data are provided:
Component surface temperature, \(T_1 = 80^\circ\mathrm{C}\)

Casing temperature, \(T_2 = 25^\circ\mathrm{C}\)

Emissivity of the component, \(\varepsilon = 0.85\)

Component surface area, \(A = 0.002\ \mathrm{m^2}\)
Calculate the heat transfer rate by radiation.
tags: Net Energy Exchange By Radiation Between Two Bodies

questions.question: A small polished metal sphere (\(\varepsilon = 0.1\)) with a surface area of \(A = 0.05\ \mathrm{m^2}\) is suspended in a large vacuum chamber. The sphere is at \(T_1 = 500\ \mathrm{K}\) and the chamber walls are at \(T_2 = 300\ \mathrm{K}\). The Stefan-Boltzmann constant is \(\sigma = 5.67 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{W/(m^2 \cdot K^4)}\). Calculate the net radiation heat loss from the sphere.
tags: Net Energy Exchange By Radiation Between Two Bodies

questions.question: A hemispherical surface (Surface 1) is placed on a flat circular base (Surface 2) to form a closed enclosure. Which of the following view factors is correct if the flat base is a non-self-viewing surface (\(F_{22} = 0\))?
tags: Shape Factor View Factor Configuration Factor Relations

questions.question:
A diffuse, opaque surface is irradiated with a total heat flux of \(G = 1,000\ \mathrm{W/m^2}\). The surface has the following properties:
Reflectivity, \(\rho = 0.35\)

Transmissivity, \(\tau = 0\) (Opaque)

The surface is assumed to be a gray body.
Calculate the emissivity (\(\varepsilon\)) of the surface.

A thin radiation shield (\(\epsilon_3 = 0.1\)) is placed between two large parallel plates. Plate 1 has \(\epsilon_1 = 0.8\) and Plate 2 has \(\epsilon_2 = 0.8\). The plates are at temperatures \(T_1 = 1000\ \mathrm{K}\) and \(T_2 = 500\ \mathrm{K}\). View Factor \(F=1\). Determine the net radiant heat flux \(\dot{q}_{12}\) between the plates with the shield in place.
tags: Net Energy Exchange By Radiation Between Two Bodies

questions.question: Two black surfaces exchange heat by radiation. Surface 1 has an area \(A_1 = 2\ \mathrm{m^2}\) and Surface 2 has an area \(A_2 = 4\ \mathrm{m^2}\). The view factor from Surface 1 to Surface 2 is \(F_{12} = 0.6\). Determine the view factor \(F_{21}\) from Surface 2 to Surface 1 using the reciprocity relation found in the NCEES FE Reference Handbook 10.5.
tags: Shape Factor View Factor Configuration Factor Relations

questions.question:
A tubular heat exchanger has the following design and operating parameters after several months of service:
Inner convection coefficient, \(h_i = 2,000\ \mathrm{W/(m^2 \cdot K)}\)

Outer convection coefficient, \(h_o = 1,500\ \mathrm{W/(m^2 \cdot K)}\)

Inner surface area, \(A_i = 0.40\ \mathrm{m^2}\)

Outer surface area, \(A_o = 0.50\ \mathrm{m^2}\)

Wall conduction resistance, \(R_{wall} = \dfrac{\ln(D_o/D_i)}{2\pi kL} = 0.0010\ \mathrm{K/W}\)

Inner fouling factor, \(R_{fi} = 0.0002\ \mathrm{m^2 \cdot K/W}\)

Outer fouling factor, \(R_{fo} = 0.0005\ \mathrm{m^2 \cdot K/W}\)
Calculate the total thermal resistance of the heat exchanger, \(1/UA\), including the effects of fouling.

A counter-flow concentric tube heat exchanger is designed such that the heat capacity rates of the hot and cold fluids are balanced (matched), meaning \(C_h = C_c\). The heat exchanger has \(NTU = 2.5\). Calculate the effectiveness (\(\varepsilon\)).

A counter-flow concentric tube heat exchanger is used for heat recovery. The following parameters are determined:
Heat capacity ratio, \(C_r = 0.60\)

Number of Transfer Units, \(NTU = 1.5\)
Calculate the effectiveness (\(\varepsilon\)) for this counter-flow arrangement.

A concentric tube heat exchanger is being analyzed for its performance. The design specifications provide the following parameters:
Overall heat transfer coefficient, \(U = 450\ \mathrm{W/(m^2 \cdot K)}\)

Heat transfer surface area, \(A = 12\ \mathrm{m^2}\)

Hot fluid mass flow rate, \(\dot{m}_h = 1.2\ \mathrm{kg/s}\) 

Hot fluid specific heat, \(c_{p,h} = 2,200\ \mathrm{J/kg \cdot K}\)

Cold fluid mass flow rate, \(\dot{m}_c = 0.8\ \mathrm{kg/s}\)

Cold fluid specific heat,\(c_{p,c} = 4,180\ \mathrm{J/kg \cdot K}\)
Calculate the Number of Transfer Units (\(NTU\)) for this heat exchanger.

A concentric tube heat exchanger is used to heat water with hot oil. To determine the maximum possible heat transfer rate, the heat capacity rates must be evaluated. The following data are provided:
Hot oil mass flow rate, \(\dot{m}_h = 0.5\ \mathrm{kg/s}\)

Hot oil specific heat, \(c_{p,h} = 2,100\ \mathrm{J/(kg \cdot K)}\)

Cold water mass flow rate, \(\dot{m}_c = 0.2\ \mathrm{kg/s}\)

Cold water specific heat, \(c_{p,c} = 4,180\ \mathrm{J/(kg \cdot K)}\)

Hot oil inlet temperature, \(T_{Hi} = 150^\circ\mathrm{C}\)

Cold water inlet temperature, \(T_{Ci} = 30^\circ\mathrm{C}\)
Calculate the maximum possible heat transfer rate, \(\dot{Q}_{max}\).

A parallel-flow heat exchanger is used to cool an exhaust gas stream using water. The temperatures at the inlets and outlets are given as follows:
Hot gas inlet temperature, \(T_{Hi} = 450^\circ\mathrm{C}\)

Hot gas outlet temperature, \(T_{Ho} = 250^\circ\mathrm{C}\)

Cold water inlet temperature, \(T_{Ci} = 40^\circ\mathrm{C}\)

Cold water outlet temperature, \(T_{Co} = 100^\circ\mathrm{C}\)
Calculate the Log Mean Temperature Difference (\(\Delta T_{lm}\)) for this parallel-flow configuration.

In a heat exchanger, a hot oil stream is used to heat a cold water stream. The heat exchanger is well-insulated from the environment. The following data are provided:
Hot oil mass flow rate, \(\dot{m}_H = 2.0\ \mathrm{kg/s}\)

Hot oil specific heat, \(c_{p,H} = 2,100\ \mathrm{J/(kg \cdot K)}\)

Hot oil inlet temperature, \(T_{Hi} = 120^\circ\mathrm{C}\)

Hot oil outlet temperature, \(T_{Ho} = 70^\circ\mathrm{C}\)

Cold water mass flow rate, \(\dot{m}_C = 1.5\ \mathrm{kg/s}\)

Cold water specific heat, \(c_{p,C} = 4,180\ \mathrm{J/(kg \cdot K)}\)

Cold water inlet temperature, \(T_{Ci} = 20^\circ\mathrm{C}\)
Calculate the outlet temperature of the cold water, \(T_{Co}\).
A parallel flow double-pipe heat exchanger has \(NTU = 2.0\) and a heat capacity ratio \(C_r = C_{min}/C_{max} = 0.5\). Calculate the effectiveness \(\epsilon\) of the heat exchanger.

A counterflow heat exchanger operates with the following temperatures: Hot fluid inlet \(T_{Hi} = 100^\circ \mathrm{C}\), Hot fluid outlet \(T_{Ho} = 60^\circ \mathrm{C}\), Cold fluid inlet \(T_{Ci} = 20^\circ \mathrm{C}\), and Cold fluid outlet \(T_{Co} = 50^\circ \mathrm{C}\). Calculate the Log-Mean Temperature Difference \(\Delta T_{lm}\).

A temperature measurement system utilizes a sensor consisting of two dissimilar conductors in electrical contact at a measured point and a reference junction. The device generates a voltage output that is proportional to the temperature difference between these two junctions. This device operates based on the:

A thermistor has a nominal resistance of \(R_0 = 10,000\ \Omega\) at \(25^\circ\text{C}\) and a \(\beta\) value of \(3950\ \text{K}\). The current measured resistance is \(R_T = 4,000\ \Omega\). The measured temperature \(T\) is most nearly:

A semiconductor thermistor has a nominal resistance of \(R_0 = 10,000\ \Omega\) at a reference temperature of \(25^\circ\text{C}\). The material-dependent value is \(\beta = 3950\ \text{K}\). The resistance of the thermistor at \(80^\circ\text{C}\) is most nearly:

A platinum RTD has a reference resistance of \(R_0 = 100\ \Omega\) at \(T_0 = 0^\circ\text{C}\) and a temperature coefficient of \(\alpha = 0.00385\ \Omega/\Omega\ \text{per}\ ^\circ\text{C}\). If the measured resistance is \(R_T = 138.5\ \Omega\), the sensed temperature \(T\) is most nearly:

A platinum Resistance Temperature Detector (RTD) has a resistance of \(R_0 = 100\ \Omega\) at a reference temperature of \(T_0 = 0^\circ\text{C}\). The resistance temperature coefficient is \(\alpha = 0.00385\ \Omega/\Omega\ \text{per}\ ^\circ\text{C}\). The resistance of the RTD at a temperature of \(T = 150^\circ\text{C}\) is most nearly:

An engineer is selecting a transducer for a dynamic measurement application. The chosen device utilizes a crystalline material that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy. Specifically, when a mechanical force is applied, the material changes dimension and an electric field is produced. This operating principle is known as the:
