questions.question: Nitrogen gas (Ideal Gas, \(R = 0.297\ \text{kJ/kg}\cdot\text{K}\), \(c_p = 1.04\ \text{kJ/kg}\cdot\text{K}\)) is compressed from \(100\ \text{kPa}, 300\ \text{K}\) to \(500\ \text{kPa}, 400\ \text{K}\). Determine the specific entropy change (\(\Delta s\)).

Calculate the Van der Waals constant \(a\) for Argon given its critical properties: \(P_c = 4.87\ \text{MPa}\), \(T_c = 150.8\ \text{K}\). Use the Universal Gas Constant \(\overline{R} = 8.314\ \text{kJ}/(\text{kmol}\cdot\text{K})\).

Determine the Van der Waals constant \(b\) for Nitrogen (\(N_2\)).The critical constants for nitrogen are \(P_c = 3.39\ \text{MPa}\) and \(T_c = 126.2\ \text{K}\). The Universal Gas Constant is \(\overline{R} = 8.314\ \text{kJ}/(\text{kmol}\cdot\text{K})\).

Nitrogen (\(N_2\)) is stored in a rigid container at a pressure of \(P = 10\ \text{MPa}\) and a temperature of \(T = 150\ \text{K}\). The critical constants for nitrogen are \(P_c = 3.39\ \text{MPa}\) and \(T_c = 126.2\ \text{K}\). The specific gas constant for nitrogen is \(R = 0.2968\ \text{kJ}/(\text{kg}\cdot\text{K})\). Using the Generalized Compressibility Chart, determine the specific volume \(v\) of the nitrogen at this state.

A laboratory chamber has interior dimensions of \(8\ \text{m} \times 5\ \text{m} \times 3\ \text{m}\). The chamber is maintained at a gage pressure of \(15\ \text{kPa}\), and the atmospheric pressure is \(100\ \text{kPa}\). The air temperature inside the chamber is \(32^\circ\text{C}\).

Assuming the molecular weight of air is \(M_{\text{air}} = 29\ \text{kg/kmol}\), determine the mass of air contained in the chamber.

A rigid air receiver (storage tank) has a volume of \(0.80\ \text{m}^3\). Initially, it contains air at an absolute pressure of \(100\ \text{kPa}\) and a temperature of  \(20^\circ\text{C}\).

A compressor then fills the tank with more air until the gage pressure in the tank is \(700\ \text{kPa}\). At the final state, the air temperature in the tank is \(60^\circ\text{C}\). 

Assuming air behaves as an ideal gas and has a molecular weight of  \(M_{\text{air}} = 28.97\ \text{kg/kmol}\), determine the mass of air added to the tank in kilograms.

A rigid pressure vessel has a fixed volume of \(3.5\ \text{m}^3\). The vessel contains nitrogen gas at an initial temperature of \(20^\circ\text{C}\) and a pressure of \(150\ \text{kPa}\). The gas is heated in the sealed vessel until the pressure reaches \(900\ \text{kPa}\). Assuming nitrogen behaves as an ideal gas and the mass in the vessel remains constant, determine the final temperature of the gas in degrees Celsius.

A high–pressure storage cylinder for compressed natural gas (CNG) has an inner diameter of \(0.30\ \text{m}\) and an internal length of \(1.2\ \text{m}\). The cylinder is initially evacuated and then filled with gas until the gage pressure reaches \(20\ \text{MPa}\) at a temperature of \(35^\circ\text{C}\).
Take the atmospheric pressure as \(100\ \text{kPa}\), and assume the gas is pure methane with molecular weight \(M = 16\ \text{kg/kmol}\). Assuming ideal-gas behavior, determine the mass of gas contained in the cylinder in kilograms.

A turbocharger compresses ambient air from an inlet pressure of \(p_1 = 95\ \text{kPa}\) to an outlet pressure of \(p_2 = 550\ \text{kPa}\) in a rapid, adiabatic, and isentropic process. The inlet air temperature is \(T_1 = 35^\circ\text{C}\). Assume that air behaves as an ideal gas with a specific heat ratio \(k = 1.4\). Determine the final air temperature in degrees Celsius.

A gas mixture is analyzed gravimetrically and found to contain 3 kg of nitrogen \((N_2)\), 5 kg of oxygen \((O_2)\), and 2 kg of carbon monoxide \((CO)\). Treating each component as an ideal gas, determine the gas constant  \(R_{\text{mix}}\) of the mixture in \(\text{kJ/(kg·K)}\).

Steam enters an adiabatic turbine at \(4\ \text{MPa}\) and \(400^\circ\text{C}\) (\(h_1 = 3214\ \text{kJ/kg}\)). The steam exits at a pressure where the isentropic enthalpy would be \(h_{2s} = 2100\ \text{kJ/kg}\). If the turbine has an isentropic efficiency of \(85\%\), determine the actual specific work output.

Two kilograms of Nitrogen gas expand in a piston-cylinder device at a constant pressure of \(500\ \text{kPa}\). The initial specific volume is \(0.1\ \text{m}^3/\text{kg}\) and the final specific volume is \(0.2\ \text{m}^3/\text{kg}\). During the process, \(150\ \text{kJ}\) of heat is added to the system. Determine the change in internal energy (\(\Delta U\)) of the nitrogen.
A) \(50\ \text{kJ}\) 

 B) \(100\ \text{kJ}\) 

 C) \(150\ \text{kJ}\) 

 D) \(250\ \text{kJ}\)

Steam enters a nozzle with an enthalpy of \(3,000\ \text{kJ/kg}\) and a velocity of \(50\ \text{m/s}\). It exits with a velocity of \(600\ \text{m/s}\). Neglecting heat transfer and potential energy, determine the specific enthalpy of the steam at the exit.
A) \(2,642\ \text{kJ/kg}\) 

 B) \(2,821\ \text{kJ/kg}\) 

 C) \(3,179\ \text{kJ/kg}\) 

 D) \(3,357\ \text{kJ/kg}\)

Air enters a compressor at \(298\ \text{K}\) and leaves at \(500\ \text{K}\). The mass flow rate of air is \(0.5\ \text{kg/s}\). Assume air behaves as an ideal gas with constant specific heats (\(C_p = 1.005\ \text{kJ/kg}\cdot\text{K}\), \(C_v = 0.718\ \text{kJ/kg}\cdot\text{K}\)). The compressor is adiabatic and kinetic/potential energy changes are negligible. Determine the power input required.
A) \(72.5\ \text{kW}\) 

 B) \(101.0\ \text{J/s}\) 

 C) \(101.5\ \text{kW}\) 

 D) \(203.0\ \text{kW}\)

Refrigerant-134a is cooled by water in a condenser (heat exchanger). The refrigerant enters at \(10\ \text{kg/min}\) with an enthalpy change of \(\Delta h_R = -150\ \text{kJ/kg}\) (loss). Cooling water enters at \(20\ \text{kg/min}\). Assume the heat exchanger is insulated from the surroundings. What is the enthalpy change of the cooling water (\(\Delta h_w\))?
A) \(30\ \text{kJ/kg}\)

B) \(75\ \text{kJ/kg}\)

C) \(150\ \text{kJ/kg}\)

D) \(300\ \text{kJ/kg}\)

Steam enters a nozzle at \(400^\circ\text{C}\) and \(800\ \text{kPa}\) with a velocity of \(10\ \text{m/s}\). It leaves at \(300\ \text{kPa}\) and \(200^\circ\text{C}\). The inlet enthalpy is \(3267\ \text{kJ/kg}\) and the exit enthalpy is \(2865\ \text{kJ/kg}\). Neglecting heat transfer and potential energy changes, determine the exit velocity of the steam.
A) \(28.4\ \text{m/s}\)

B) \(804\ \text{m/s}\)

C) \(897\ \text{m/s}\)

D) \(804,000\ \text{m/s}\)

Refrigerant-134a flows through a throttling valve. Assuming the process is adiabatic and potential/kinetic energy changes are negligible, which property remains constant across the valve?
A) Pressure

B) Temperature

C) Enthalpy

D) Entropy

A closed piston-cylinder device contains a gas. During a process, \(50\ \text{kJ}\) of heat is added to the system, and the system does \(20\ \text{kJ}\) of work on the surroundings. What is the change in internal energy (\(\Delta U\)) of the system?
A) \(-30\ \text{kJ}\)

B) \(30\ \text{kJ}\)

C) \(70\ \text{kJ}\)

D) \(-70\ \text{kJ}\)

Steam enters an adiabatic turbine at a rate of \(10\ \text{kg/s}\). The inlet enthalpy is \(h_{i} = 3200\ \text{kJ/kg}\), and the exit enthalpy is \(h_{e} = 2100\ \text{kJ/kg}\). Neglecting changes in kinetic and potential energy, determine the power output of the turbine.
A) \(1,100\ \text{kW}\)

B) \(-11,000\ \text{kW}\)

C) \(11,000\ \text{kW}\)

D) \(53,000\ \text{kW}\)

One kilogram of saturated water–steam mixture is initially at \(70^\circ\text{C}\) with a quality of \(x = 0.25\). From the steam table, the saturation pressure at \(70^\circ\text{C}\) is \(31.19\ \text{kPa}\) and the specific volumes are  \(v_f = 0.001023\ \text{m}^3/\text{kg}\) and \(v_g = 5.042\ \text{m}^3/\text{kg}\). The mixture is heated at this constant pressure of \(31.19\ \text{kPa}\) until the temperature reaches \(200^\circ\text{C}\), at which point the steam is superheated. For the superheated state, assume ideal-gas behavior with \(R = 0.4615\ \text{kPa·m}^3/(\text{kg·K}) \). Using ideal-gas approximation for the final state, determine the work done (kJ) during the constant-pressure heating process.

A vertical cylinder with an inner diameter of \(0.12\ \text{m}\) initially contains  \(150\ \text{cm}^3\) of water at \(70^\circ\text{C}\). A \(40\ \text{kg}\) frictionless piston rests on top of the water and is exposed to the atmosphere. The system is slowly heated until the water temperature reaches \(220^\circ\text{C}\). Assume the following:
Atmospheric pressure: \(p_{\text{atm}} = 101\ \text{kPa}\)

Water at \(70^\circ\text{C}\) behaves as a compressed liquid with  \(v_f(70^\circ\text{C}) = 0.00103\ \text{m}^3/\text{kg}\)

The final state at \(220^\circ\text{C}\) is superheated steam that can be approximated as an ideal gas with \(R = 0.4615\ \text{kPa·m}^3/(\text{kg·K})\)
Determine the work in kJ done by the water during this process.

In an ideal Rankine cycle, steam leaves the boiler at \(h_3 = 3200\ \text{kJ/kg}\) and enters the condenser at \(h_4 = 2100\ \text{kJ/kg}\). The enthalpy of water leaving the condenser is \(h_1 = 200\ \text{kJ/kg}\), and the work input to the pump is \(5\ \text{kJ/kg}\) (so \(h_2 = 205\ \text{kJ/kg}\)). Determine the thermal efficiency of the cycle.
The ideal Otto cycle consists of four processes. Which of the following correctly describes the heat addition and heat rejection processes in this cycle?

choices.A: Constant Pressure Heat Addition, Constant Volume Heat Rejection
choices.B: Constant Volume Heat Addition, Constant Pressure Heat Rejection
choices.C: Constant Volume Heat Addition, Constant Volume Heat Rejection
choices.D: Constant Pressure Heat Addition, Constant Pressure Heat Rejection

If the environmental dead state temperature is \(T_L = 298\ \text{K}\), determine the Irreversibility (\(I\)) of this process.

Steam enters a turbine with a specific enthalpy \(h = 3200\ \text{kJ/kg}\) and specific entropy \(s = 7.0\ \text{kJ/kg}\cdot\text{K}\). The environmental “dead state” conditions are \(T_L = 298\ \text{K}\) (\(25^\circ\text{C}\)), \(P_L = 100\ \text{kPa}\), \(h_L = 105\ \text{kJ/kg}\), and \(s_L = 0.36\ \text{kJ/kg}\cdot\text{K}\). Neglecting kinetic and potential energy, calculate the specific flow exergy (availability, \(\Psi\)) of the steam at the inlet.

choices.A: The claim is valid because it satisfies the First Law of Thermodynamics (Energy Conservation).
choices.B: The claim is invalid because it violates the Kelvin-Planck statement of the Second Law.
choices.C: The claim is invalid because it violates the Clausius statement of the Second Law.
choices.D: The claim is valid if the engine operates reversibly.

Given Standard Enthalpies of Formation (\(\Delta H_f^\circ\)):
\(CO(g) = -110.5\ \text{kJ/mol}\)
